assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Z2 topological classification of time-reversal-invariant insulators, the quantum spin Hall effect and its realization with protected edge states opened a new field in electronic-structure and band-topology physics. It is original, conceptually clean, and has had enormous lasting influence on materials theory, including first-principles identification of topological materials.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the decisive theory (quantum spin Hall effect in graphene and the Z2 invariant); Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental realization in HgTe wells. This forms a natural theory-plus-experiment trio. Other contributors to the HgTe proposal and the 3D generalization (for example Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu, Moore, Hasan) are not in the supplied credit list, so the allocation is not fully resolved.
assessment.maturity: More than fifteen years of independent confirmation across HgTe, InAs/GaSb, Bi-based and other materials; the interpretation is stable and the field is mature, so recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with candidate B002, which includes quantum anomalous Hall experiments, so the scope of the discovery could be framed in more than one way.
Priority disputes over the quantum spin Hall proposal and the 3D topological insulators may complicate a three-person prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle in twisted bilayer graphene, followed by the observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states, created moire quantum matter as a tunable platform for correlated electrons. The work is highly original and its first-principles and continuum-model understanding is of central interest to the electronic-structure community.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key band-structure prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery of correlated and superconducting phases. This is a coherent theory-plus-experiment configuration, although others (for example Dean, Yacoby, Young, Kim for related moire and heterostructure work) are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Strongly replicated in many groups since 2018, but the origin of superconductivity and the nature of correlated states are still debated; the field is young, so a prize is arguably slightly early yet well justified.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity and the nature of the correlated phases remain unresolved.
Credit relative to the broader moire and van der Waals heterostructure community is not fully settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory gave the first controlled and practical non-perturbative framework for strongly correlated electrons, explaining the Mott transition and, combined with density functional theory, enabling quantitative materials calculations. Its importance across correlated-electron physics is very high and its impact is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Georges and Kotliar developed the exact mapping to an impurity model and the DFT+DMFT program; Vollhardt contributed the infinite-dimension framework with Metzner. Walter Metzner and Muller-Hartmann are not in the supplied credit, which leaves a real attribution gap, but the three listed names form a defensible group.
assessment.maturity: Decades of use and validation against experiment in oxides, f-electron systems and iron-based superconductors; mature. Limits in cluster extensions and quantitative predictivity are known.
uncertainties: Omission of Metzner and Muller-Hartmann from the credited list makes allocation uncertain.
A theory-method prize competes against experimental discoveries for the physics prize emphasis.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Giant tunnel magnetoresistance in crystalline MgO junctions combined first-principles prediction of coherent spin-dependent tunnelling with experimental realization, and underpins modern hard-disk read heads and magnetic random-access memory. It is a clear case where electronic-structure calculation guided a technologically important discovery.
assessment.attribution: Butler and Mathon predicted the effect from band-structure calculations; Yuasa and Parkin independently realized large room-temperature TMR in MgO junctions in 2004. The credit set is well matched, though Mathon is not listed and Djayaprawira/Tsunekawa and others contributed to related results.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with two decades of industrial use and independent confirmation; timely, and fairly close in kind to the earlier giant magnetoresistance prize.
uncertainties: Possible concern that the topic is too close to the 2007 giant magnetoresistance prize.
Priority interplay between Yuasa and Parkin and the missing co-author on the theory side.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration correction in electron lenses broke a decades-old resolution limit and made routine sub-angstrom imaging and spectroscopy of atoms in solids possible. The invention is concrete, original and has transformed materials physics, including direct testing of calculated atomic and electronic structure.
assessment.attribution: Rose provided the theory of aberration correction, Haider and Urban built and demonstrated the corrector for the transmission electron microscope and scanning versions; the three-person group is natural. Others such as Krivanek, Dellby and Zach built competing correctors and are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with widespread use for over twenty years and unambiguous demonstration. Recognition is timely; physics content versus engineering is a possible debate.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as primarily instrumentation rather than a discovery.
Competing contributions by the scanning transmission electron microscope corrector community are not credited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of strong magnetoelectric coupling and magnetically driven ferroelectricity in frustrated magnets and in thin-film multiferroics showed new couplings between spin and charge order. As a magnetism theorist I find the underlying microscopic mechanisms important and the field intellectually rich, though application impact has so far been more modest.
assessment.attribution: Tokura and Cheong led the discovery of spin-driven ferroelectricity in TbMnO3-type compounds, and Ramesh led the epitaxial thin-film route with BiFeO3. Theoretical contributors (for example Spaldin, Katsura, Nagaosa, Sergienko, Dagotto) are not credited, so the experimental trio would receive credit while theory credit remains unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Well established with broad confirmation, but practical use in devices has been limited and the interpretation of magnetoelectric mechanisms continues to evolve; recognition would be reasonable but not urgent.
uncertainties: Device impact has not matched early expectations.
Theory contributors are missing from the credit and could be viewed as essential.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proposals and demonstrations for quantum computation and simulation with trapped ions and neutral atoms established controllable many-body quantum platforms, with lasting impact across quantum information and many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller proposed the trapped-ion quantum computer and many later schemes; Blatt demonstrated key ion-trap protocols with high fidelity. Bloch is also credited for optical-lattice work, but I select the three with the cleanest gate-and-simulation link. Wineland's earlier prize covers part of the ion-trap field, which complicates allocation.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed, with growing scale; but the field is moving quickly and overlaps with prior prizes (2012, 2022), so the novelty of the recognition and the right dividing line are uncertain.
uncertainties: Overlap with already recognized trapped-ion and entanglement work.
Compound discovery: ions and neutral atoms may merit different recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, using magic-wavelength trapping, delivers the most precise measurements of time and frequency and supports tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and searches for new physics. The concept is original and the experimental performance is dramatic.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and demonstrated the magic-wavelength lattice clock; Ye brought it to extreme precision and many-body spin-physics regimes. A two-person prize is clean, with other clock groups (for example Lemke, Ludlow, Hinkley) not credited.
assessment.maturity: Mature with repeated confirmation across laboratories; timely, but the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 prize on trapped ions set a context where the added novelty must be judged carefully.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with previous precision-measurement prizes.
A redefinition of the second has not yet occurred, so full impact is still developing.
